rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.sdk.graph.node_content.fingerprint`. I judged this from the supplied test sources and did not request implementation source.

The subject has three testable obligations, plus a process rule about changing the scheme.

1. **Fingerprint describes the retained contents and makes no further reads.**
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot]` reads a snapshot, then changes the underlying contents from "before" to "after".
   - It asserts that `snapshot.content.fingerprint()` still equals `snapshot.fingerprint`, and that `format()` still returns "before".
   - It also asserts that the read log is exactly `[1]`, so no extra resource read happened.
   - `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirement_edges_and_input_freshness_use_the_sdk]` does the same on the Habeas domain.
   - It retains a reference set and a source node, then edits `src/lib.rs` on disk.
   - It asserts that the retained fingerprints are unchanged after the edit.
   - A fresh read of the changed state gives a different fingerprint. That rules out an implementation that re-reads mutable state, or one whose fingerprint ignores the content.

2. **The same contents under the same rules give the same fingerprint.**
   - In the SDK test, `domain.node_content(...)` on the input selector gives a fingerprint equal to the earlier `ctx.read(...)` of the same selector. That is a separate read of the same contents.
   - The test also pins a golden digest, `a60363aa…`, under the scheme `habeas-input-v1`. This shows the result is deterministic.
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[wildcard_versions_still_check_inputs_and_errors]` checks that a record is current when the stored fingerprint matches the freshly read one.
   - The same test shows it is not current when the contents change (`fp("changed")`).
   - It also shows it is not current when only the scheme differs (`Fingerprint::new("other", "same")`), so both scheme and digest take part in comparison.

3. **Retain everything needed to describe the observation, including its rules and version.**
   - The reference-set fingerprint is asserted to equal `Fingerprint::new("habeas-reference-set-v1", <reference_set>)`.
   - The input fingerprint is asserted to carry the scheme `habeas-input-v1`.
   - Both pin the scheme and digest values, so a change in rules without a change in scheme would break the golden values.

4. **"When the rules change, change the scheme."** This is a maintenance rule. The pinned scheme and digest assertions are the only practical check.

All three test functions carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no marking gap and no unacknowledged gap.
